out.other_title: Debater strength (Elo) vs judge accuracy and correct-answer advantage in debate
out.rationale: The authors explicitly state consistency with prior work including Kenton et al., which they describe as finding that judge accuracy may improve with using better models. Kenton et al. report that, with Pro 1.5 as judge, stronger debaters have higher aggregate Elo and lead to higher judge accuracy on extractive tasks, with less differentiation on closed tasks. The citing work finds that the Guard's (judge's) performance scales with general intelligence rating while Houdini performance stays constant, so it varies the judge where Kenton et al. vary the debaters.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: Whether debate judge accuracy improves with stronger models; Engels et al. vary the judge (Guard), whose performance scales with general intelligence rating on TruthfulQA, with similar scaling on QuALITY and PrOntoQA and mostly flat performance on BoolQ, while Kenton et al. vary the debaters with Pro 1.5 as judge and find higher judge accuracy on extractive tasks but less differentiation on closed tasks; per Engels et al., prior work including Kenton et al. tests only a few models, and the Guard's 'performance' against general intelligence rating is not shown to be the same measure as Kenton et al.'s judge accuracy against debater aggregate Elo

text: The authors find that on TruthfulQA their debate judge's (Guard's) performance scales with general intelligence rating, with similar scaling on QuALITY and PrOntoQA but mostly flat performance for both Guards and Houdinis on BoolQ. They state that their observations are consistent with Kenton et al. (2024), who find that judge accuracy may improve with better models, and add that the explicit comparison between different judges had not been undertaken in prior work.
title: Debate judge (Guard) scaling on TruthfulQA is consistent with Kenton et al.'s finding that better models may improve judge accuracy
